text:
Here are several **Washington-licensed clinicians who advertise online treatment for trichotillomania (hair pulling), excoriation disorder/skin picking, or other body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs):**

- **Jeanette Lantz, PhD — CBT Northwest**  
  Offers **online videotherapy exclusively** to clients in Washington and California. Uses CBT, **habit-reversal training (HRT)**, ERP, mindfulness, and ACT for skin picking and hair pulling. Based in Tacoma. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/providers/lantz-jeanette/?utm_source=openai))

- **Tamara Harrison, LMHC, CMHS — Evergreen State Counseling**  
  Provides online individual therapy, support groups, and programs focused on OCD and BFRBs, including skin picking and hair pulling. Her IOCDF listing says her practice is devoted to OCD, anxiety, BFRBs, and related disorders. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/providers/harrison-tamara/?utm_source=openai))

- **Lisa Shaw, PhD — Seattle Anxiety & OCD**  
  Offers remote telehealth to people currently located anywhere in Washington and lists trichotillomania, skin picking, CBT, behavior therapy, and HRT-related approaches among her specialties. ([seattleanxietyocd.com](https://www.seattleanxietyocd.com/?utm_source=openai))

- **Meghan Keough, PhD — Pacific Northwest Therapy**  
  Provides telehealth and treats trichotillomania and other BFRBs using CBT, ERP, and habit-reversal approaches. Based in Edmonds. ([hoarding.iocdf.org](https://hoarding.iocdf.org/providers/keough-meghan/?utm_source=openai))

- **Tory Lincoln, PhD — Lincoln Psychology**  
  Offers telehealth to clients physically located in Washington and treats children, teens, young adults, and adults with trichotillomania and skin picking. ([lincolnpsychology.com](https://www.lincolnpsychology.com/?utm_source=openai))

- **David J. Kosins, PhD**  
  Listed by the TLC Foundation as a Washington-licensed psychologist treating adult trichotillomania, skin picking, and other BFRBs with CBT; teletherapy is available. ([bfrb.org](https://www.bfrb.org/medical-therapeutic-providers/david-j.-kosins?utm_source=openai))

- **Jacqueline Randall, PsyD — Northwest CBT**  
  Washington-licensed provider treating adults with hair pulling, skin picking, and other BFRBs using comprehensive behavioral treatment. Ask directly whether she currently offers video appointments and accepts new clients. ([bfrb.org](https://www.bfrb.org/medical-therapeutic-providers/jacqueline-randall?utm_source=openai))

- **Brian Thompson, PhD — Portland Psychotherapy**  
  Although based in Oregon, he states that he is licensed for telehealth with clients residing in Washington and treats trichotillomania and skin picking using CBT/ACT-oriented approaches. ([portlandpsychotherapy.com](https://portlandpsychotherapy.com/our-team/brian-thompson/?utm_source=openai))

### How to choose

When contacting them, ask:

1. **Do you specifically use HRT, Comprehensive Behavioral Treatment for BFRBs (ComB), or the TLC Foundation’s evidence-based BFRB protocols?**
2. Do you treat **skin picking/hair pulling directly**, rather than only general anxiety or OCD?
3. Do you see your age group and offer video sessions throughout Washington?
4. Are you in-network, out-of-network, or private pay?
5. Do you have experience with bald spots, wounds, scarring, hair eating, or severe skin damage if relevant?

The **TLC Foundation provider directory** and **International OCD Foundation directory** are good places to find additional specialists; their listings can change, so confirm current licensure, availability, fees, and insurance before scheduling. If picking has caused deep wounds, spreading redness, pus, fever, or significant bleeding, also contact a primary-care clinician or urgent care.
